Access._comment: Development only. The signing key is in a file here so the thing runs out of the box; anywhere real it belongs in user secrets or an environment variable, because whoever holds it can mint a token for anybody with any permission. The bootstrap administrator is created once, on an empty users table, and must change this password on first sign-in.

Security._comment: Development only, and the same rule as the signing key above: this key is in a file so the thing runs out of the box, and anywhere real it belongs in user secrets or an environment variable, because whoever holds it can read every encrypted column in the database. Generating a real one is one line, and it has to come from a cryptographic generator rather than Get-Random: [Convert]::ToBase64String([System.Security.Cryptography.RandomNumberGenerator]::GetBytes(32))
